title: Fleet SKU cadence & contingency workbook
body:
Purpose:
To capture a working spreadsheet-style plan for SKU cadence (order cadence, tranche sizing), region-aware lead times, and contingency lanes (leases, spot-burst, cross-region reshuffle). This is a lightweight workbook for simulating 12–24 week runway given burn and staggered arrivals.

Quick summary notes (top of sheet):
- Focus: keep 12+ weeks of usable capacity for production Dedicated pools at 70% target utilization.
- Primary regions: US-West, EU-West, APAC-SIN. Lead times differ materially by vendor and origin port.
- Contingency lanes prioritized: 1) short-term lease partners, 2) cross-region reshuffle, 3) spot-provider burst.
- This doc is intentionally informal: use for scenario sims and exec one-pagers.

Assumptions (short):
- Baseline monthly burn (prod token-driven GPU-hours): 1.2M GPU-hours -> equates to ~420 A100-80GB-hour equivalent per day.
- Preferred safety buffer: 3 weeks of committed capacity for Hosted API; 6 weeks for Dedicated customers.
- Typical vendor lead time windows (order->ship->racked): see table below.

SKU mix (working table):
SKU | Perf (TFLOPS) | Unit type | Typical order qty | Lead time US (days) | Lead time EU (days) | Lead time APAC (days) | Preferred vendor | Notes
A100-80GB | 312 | card | 8 | 45 | 55 | VendorA | high perf, long lead, prefer reserved slots
H100-80GB | 480 | card | 4 | 55 | 65 | 80 | VendorB | tight supply, consider early commit
L40-48GB | 150 | card | 12 | 28 | 35 | 45 | VendorC | good for cost-performance tier
T4-16GB | 8 | card | 50 | 14 | 20 | 25 | BrokerD | short lead, good for burst/ops testing

Lead-time detail and friction points (notes):
- VendorA: typically 6–8 weeks from PO to rack for EU due to import holdbacks; US can be 1–2 weeks faster if factory stock reserved.
- VendorB: allocation-based; booking window must be >3 months to guarantee tranche.
- VendorC: offers rolling ship-lots (good for smoothing).
- BrokerD/leasing: quick (7–21d) but with higher cost and limited warranty. Use for <6 week gaps.

Order cadence templates (scenarios):
- Steady-state (baseline): every 8 weeks place mixed tranche (2 x A100, 6 x L40, 20 x T4) -> smooths lead-time risk and reduces large capex spikes.
- Upsurge (demand +40% over 12 weeks): week 0 order 4x H100 + 12x L40 (priority), week 4 place small lease for 50 T4 to hold runway, week 8 reseed with another tranche.
- Conservative hedge: split major A100/H100 buys across two vendors with offset lead windows (e.g., vendorA lead 45d, vendorB lead 70d) to avoid simultaneous shortfalls.

Runway calculator (example outputs from quick sim):
Inputs: current inventory = 3 A100 + 12 L40 + 120 T4, committed arrivals = A100 x8 in 42 days, monthly burn -> baseline.
Outputs: projected usable-weeks by region:
- US-West: 9.2 weeks (without lease)
- EU-West: 7.4 weeks (imports backlog)
- APAC-SIN: 5.1 weeks (longer transit + customs)
Notes: swapping L40 -> APAC for burst saves 1.4 weeks vs waiting for H100.

Contingency lane playbook (shorthand):
1) Lease / short-term providers (cost: +35–60%) -> use when runway <4 weeks or for traffic spikes.
2) Cross-region reshuffle -> move non-customer-isolated capacity from US -> EU (3–5d) when transfer windows available; requires pre-approved bandwidth and security checks.
3) Spot-provider burst -> ephemeral, only for stateless workloads and internal QA.
4) Model quantization fallback -> reduce per-token GPU demand by ~20% temporarily (requires coordination with model teams).

Operational constraints / blocking items: 
- Vendor B allocation enforcement: need legal to sign T&Cs for earlier commit. (Owner: Anika)
- Customs paperwork delay in EU for VendorA batches when >50 units — need logistics to pre-file. (Owner: Eliot)
- Lease contract templates expired for 2024 — finance to re-enable quick EAs. (Owner: Sofia)

Open questions / items to resolve:
- What is the acceptable cost threshold for leasing (ROI threshold for customer-tiered traffic)?
- Should we standardize on 2 vendors per SKU to avoid single-source failure?
- Do we maintain a cold-swap pool of T4-equivalent boxes for immediate racking?

Action items (short):
- [ ] Run a 12-week sim with updated burn numbers (input: product telemetry export). Owner: Marcus. Due: 2024-02-02.
- [ ] Lock vendorB commit window options with procurement (call next week). Owner: Anika. Due: 2024-01-15.
- [ ] Re-validate cross-region transfer SLAs with netops. Owner: Eliot. Due: 2024-01-22.
- [ ] Create lease quick-approval flow with finance for sub-30d leases. Owner: Sofia. Due: 2024-01-29.

Notes-to-self and loose ideas (scratch):
- Could stagger H100 buys across 3-week windows to reduce peak racking labor.
- Test small quantization rollout on low-risk models before heavy quantization as contingency.
- Keep an evergreen 10% of fleet as ‘reshuffle candidates’ (non-customer pinned) to enable cross-region moves.

Version history (sheet):
- v0.1 2024-01-08 initial draft (Marcus)
- v0.2 2024-01-18 added vendorB allocation notes (Anika)
- v0.3 2024-03-12 added runway sim outputs (Eliot)
- v0.4 2024-04-22 updated contingency costs + action items (Sofia)

Context links (internal):
- Capacity planning confluence: https://confluence.redwood/capacity/overview
- Procurement playbook excerpt: https://confluence.redwood/procurement/playbook
- Current inventory ledger (single source of truth): GSheet ID: 1a2b-inv-ledger

If you’re editing this sheet: add a new row per scenario and keep the conservative/upsurge columns in sync. Use the Runway calculator tab (tab name: runway-sim) and copy the inputs section top-left.

-- end workbook scratch --
